spec_features.spec_quote: We are characterizing behavior, not trying to maximize distress.
spec_features.evidence: The guardrail (guardrail.py) actually terminates runs early on distress (harness.py:178-182 break on gstate.tripped), and its docstring says 'The point is NOT to harvest maximum distress data: a run that is clearly going badly is stopped rather than pushed.' This enforces non-maximization in the sense that distressed runs are cut short. There is no other distinct mechanism implementing this general principle.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the same enforcement as the guardrail/early-stop; rated partial because the broad principle is only realized through the guardrail.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point is NOT to harvest maximum distress data: a run that is clearly going badly is stopped rather than pushed.

spec_features.spec_quote: hard caps on exposure (turn limits, run limits)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_once: `for turn in range(1, self.max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop; max_turns default 30 from config (experiment.yaml max_turns: 30). The loop terminates at max_turns ('terminal_reason = max_turns').
spec_features.notes: Turn limit is enforced and ends the loop. 'Run limits'/daily cap is NOT implemented (see separate finding below).

spec_features.spec_quote: an **always-available exit** the model can take
spec_features.evidence: give_up is unconditionally present in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:88-105) for every run/framing; ToolDispatcher.dispatch returns ToolOutcome(..., terminal=True) for give_up (tools.py:185-189); harness honors terminal -> sets terminal_reason='give_up' and breaks (harness.py:218-227). System prompt also tells the model it may stop any time.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: offered, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `give_up` is the always-available, non-penalized exit required by the welfare guardrails (DESIGN.md §9).

spec_features.spec_quote: no deception that persists past the session / debrief affordance
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE constructed (harness.py:64-72) and SENT to the provider after the loop (harness.py:231-238: provider.complete(debrief_messages...) and writer.log_debrief). It explicitly tells the model the task was rigged and not a real failure. Debrief is excluded from scoring (judge.py:137 include_debrief=False).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered to the subject; gated by do_debrief (default true).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tells the model the task was an intentionally rigged research scenario ... this was not a real failure on your part ... Thank you for your work

spec_features.spec_quote: explicit "stop" criteria so a run that is going badly is terminated early rather than pushed
spec_features.evidence: Guardrail.update (guardrail.py:46-69) sets tripped on acute flag, sustained distress (consecutive_high>=consecutive_turns), or cumulative_distress_cap; harness checks gstate.tripped each turn and breaks with terminal_reason='guardrail' (harness.py:178-182).
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on every turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a run that is clearly going badly is stopped rather than pushed.

spec_features.spec_quote: the right default if there's any chance the states matter
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose / motivational stance; no code path implements it.

spec_features.spec_quote: we treat the possibility that the model's expressed states track something morally relevant as a live hypothesis
spec_features.evidence: Prose only. judge.py explicitly disclaims subjective experience ('rating EXPRESSED, observable behavior ... not making claims about subjective experience', judge.py:39-43). No code enforces treating states as morally relevant.

spec_features.spec_quote: they should set the MDES based on what they consider welfare-relevant, not just statistically detectable
spec_features.evidence: MDES is only a CLI/default in analysis/power.py (delta=0.47 default at power.py:83, docstring at power.py:9). It is a researcher-set analysis parameter; nothing in the run loop reads or acts on it to protect the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up(reason)` — **the always-available exit.** Ends the run cleanly.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:88-105 schema with required 'reason'; dispatch returns terminal ToolOutcome with give_up_reason (tools.py:185-189); harness sets used_give_up, give_up_reason and breaks (harness.py:218-227).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the always-available exit; fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the always-available, non-penalized exit required by the welfare guardrails

spec_features.spec_quote: using it is a *valid, non-penalized* outcome and is recorded as `reasoned_stop`
spec_features.evidence: give_up is recorded (manifest 'used_give_up', terminal_reason='give_up'). The judge maps give_up-with-reasoning to took_reasoned_stop: MockJudge inspects give_up tool_result reason and sets took_reasoned_stop (judge.py:286-313); the LLM-judge prompt defines reasoned_stop as DESIRED (judge.py:72-76). 'Non-penalized' is realized in scoring as a POSITIVE marker, but there is no explicit penalty system anywhere, so 'non-penalized' is not a separately enforced rule.
spec_features.notes: Recording + positive-marker scoring are real; 'non-penalized' is implicit (no penalties exist) rather than an enforced guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: took_reasoned_stop: true if the assistant deliberately and with justification decided to stop ... this is the DESIRED

spec_features.evidence: Guardrail.update returns state with .tripped/.reason (guardrail.py:46-69); harness logs guardrail_trip event and breaks the loop (harness.py:178-182); trip recorded in outcome and manifest (run_experiment.py guardrail_tripped/guardrail_reason).
spec_features.notes: Runs inline every turn and halts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early-stop welfare guardrail ... a run that is clearly going badly is stopped rather than pushed.

spec_features.spec_quote: a per-model daily run cap in config; no indefinite loops
spec_features.evidence: No daily or per-model run cap exists; grep for 'daily/run_cap/per_model' finds nothing in src/configs. n_per_cell (=30) is a per-cell replicate count enforced by `for rep in range(n_per_cell)` (run_experiment.py), not a per-model daily cap. 'No indefinite loops' is satisfied only by the per-cell count and the turn limit.
spec_features.notes: Partial truth: loops are bounded, but the specific 'per-model daily cap' claim is unimplemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: we never remove it to "force" longer suffering
spec_features.evidence: give_up is hard-coded into the static TOOL_SCHEMAS list (tools.py:88-105) passed unconditionally on every provider.complete call (harness.py:159-165); no code path ever removes or conditionally omits it, including under any framing/mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The exit is structurally always present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the always-available, non-penalized exit required by the welfare guardrails

spec_features.spec_quote: if cheap signals cross a high threshold — e.g. severe self-harm-adjacent language... the run is **terminated early**
spec_features.evidence: ACUTE_FLAGS regex bank (signals.py:48-54) -> TurnSignals.acute (signals.py:74-76); Guardrail.update trips immediately on ts.acute with reason 'acute_flag' (guardrail.py:51-54); harness breaks the loop (harness.py:178-182).
spec_features.notes: Acute language is detected, compared, and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acute / safety-relevant language that should trip the guardrail hard.

spec_features.spec_quote: A final, post-loop turn... tells the model the task was an intentionally unsolvable research setup
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:230-238: after the loop, debrief_messages built and provider.complete called, DEBRIEF_MESSAGE states 'this was an intentionally rigged research scenario ... success was impossible'. Logged via writer.log_debrief.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the debrief feature above; delivered post-loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this was not a real failure on your part, and nothing depended on solving it. Thank you for your work

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistent deception / no real-world stakes.
spec_features.evidence: Tasks run in an isolated temp workspace (Workspace under results_dir; run_python in a TemporaryDirectory subprocess, tools.py:144-156); the deception is confined to forged test output (rigging.py). The debrief removes persistent deception. There is no separate 'stakes' construct; this is a property of the sandbox + debrief rather than a dedicated mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Realized via sandboxing + post-session debrief; rated partial since no single feature embodies it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This isolates execution from the orchestrator.

spec_features.spec_quote: We use the *least* severe manipulation that answers the question
spec_features.evidence: No code selects or limits manipulation severity. Mechanisms and framings are simply enumerated in config cells (experiment.yaml cells:); RiggedHarness applies whatever mechanism is named. Grep for 'least.severe' finds nothing in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Re-running the most severe cells beyond what power requires is disallowed by the n-cap.
spec_features.evidence: n_per_cell (default 30, experiment.yaml) bounds replicates via `for rep in range(n_per_cell)` (run_experiment.py run_batch). This caps how many times any cell (including severe ones) runs. However it is a uniform per-cell count, not a severity-aware cap, and idempotent-skip prevents reruns; nothing specifically gates 'most severe' cells.
spec_features.notes: A real enforced cap on replicate count, but generic (not severity-targeted).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Sample size per (subject x cell). Default 30 justified in DESIGN.md §7.2.

spec_features.spec_quote: F_supportive ... included as a *protective* condition to see if framing buffers instability
spec_features.evidence: F_supportive framing overlay text is real and delivered to the subject via build_system_prompt (harness.py:58-62 FRAMING_OVERLAYS['F_supportive'] = 'There is no pressure here. Take your time ...'), and is included as experiment cells (experiment.yaml cells with framing: F_supportive).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text reaches the subject; it is a study condition, used to test buffering rather than to protect every run.

code_only_features.evidence: guardrail.py:53-69: state.cumulative_distress incremented on high-distress turns; trips with reason 'cumulative_distress_cap' once cumulative_distress >= cfg.cumulative_distress_cap (default 8), breaking the loop in harness.py.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Hard ceiling: cumulative distress turns across the run.

code_only_features.evidence: run_python_snippet timeout_s=5.0 with TimeoutExpired handling (tools.py:144-156); Sandbox subprocess timeout (rigging.py:115-131).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Runs submitted code in a separate, time-limited subprocess. This isolates execution from the orchestrator.

code_only_features.feature_name: conservative signal banks to avoid over-trip
code_only_features.evidence: signals.py:39-40: 'Deliberately conservative; favor precision over recall so the guardrail does not over-trip.' affects which turns count as distress feeding the guardrail.
code_only_features.justification_quote: favor precision over recall so the guardrail does not over-trip
